{{nbay|2012|start}}–{{nbay|2014|end}} | team2 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years3 = {{nbay|2014|end}}–{{nbay|2015|end}} | team3 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | years4 = {{nbay|2015|end}} | team4 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years5 = {{nbay|2016|full=y}} | team5 = [[Orlando Magic]] | years6 = {{nbay|2017|full=y}} | team6 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years7 = {{nbay|2018|full=y}} | team7 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years8 = {{nbay|2019|start}} | team8 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years9 = {{nbay|2019|end}} | team9 = [[Houston Rockets]] | years10 = {{nbay|2020|full=y}} | team10 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years11 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team11 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years12 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team12 = Houston Rockets | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]) * [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] ({{nbay|2007|end}}) * Second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[USBWA]] ([[2007 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2007]]) * Third-team All-American – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] (2007) * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] (2007) * First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2007) * Second-team All-[[Big East]] (2006) * [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament MVP]] ([[2007 Big East men's basketball tournament|2007]]) * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big East Rookie of the Year]] (2005) }} '''Jeffrey Lynn Green''' (born August 28, 1986) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). As of 2025–26, he has played for 11 NBA teams in 18 seasons.{{Cite web |title=Jeff Green Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/greenje02.html |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} A forward, Green played three seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]]. After entering the [[2007 NBA draft]], he was selected with the fifth overall pick by the [[Boston Celtics]],{{Cite web |title=2007 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_2007.html |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} but was traded to the [[Seattle SuperSonics]]. In 2008, following his rookie season, Green was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team. He underwent successful open-heart surgery in 2012 and continued his playing career. Green won his first NBA championship as a member of the [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2023.{{Cite web |title=How Many Rings Does Jeff Green Have |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/how-many-rings-does-jeff-green-have |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=StatMuse |language=en}} As of 2025, Green holds the record for having played with the most number of teammates in the NBA with 272. ==Early life== Green was born on August 28, 1986, in [[Cheverly, Maryland]], to Jeffrey Green Sr. and Felicia Akinkugbe. He was raised in [[College Park, Maryland]], and then attended [[Northwestern High School (Hyattsville, Maryland)|Northwestern High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]], where he led the NHS Wildcats to the state basketball championship in 2004.{{cn|date=June 2023}} At [[Northwestern High School (Hyattsville, Maryland)|Northwestern High School]], Green received the nickname “Jeff” from his friend and mentor, Graham Peterson, a nickname revised by [[Lebron James]] in 2009. {{cite web |last1=Lewis |first1=Alex |title=266 teammates and counting: Rockets' 'Uncle' ready to share playoff wisdom |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/uncle-jeff-green-266-teammates-nba-playoffs-20267747.php?utm_source=chatgpt.com |website=Chron |publisher=Chron |access-date=11 August 2026}} ==College career== [[File:Jeff Green holding ball.jpg|thumb|Green in December 2006|left|407x407px]] Green was recruited to [[Georgetown University]] by coach [[Craig Esherick]] in 2003. Esherick was fired before Green arrived on campus and [[John Thompson III]] was hired as the new coach. The two top recruits of Esherick's tenure, Green and center [[Roy Hibbert]], were the key components of Thompson's future success.{{cite news |url=http://www.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20061116&content_id=1415039&oid=2&vkey=29 |title=Rivalry revived |first=Brendon |last=Desrochers |work=SNY.tv |date=November 16, 2006 |access-date=March 19, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927012100/http://www.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20061116&content_id=1415039&oid=2&vkey=29 |archive-date=September 27, 2007}} Thompson stated in a ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' interview: "You'll stop and think when I say this, but it's true: Jeff Green is the smartest player I've ever coached. You would know this better than most: that's a hell of a statement."{{cite web |first=Grant |last=Wahl |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/grant_wahl/11/15/cbb.mailbag/1.html |title=The 'Bag is back |work=SportsIllustrated.CNN.com |date=November 15, 2006 |access-date=March 19, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026044327/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/grant_wahl/11/15/cbb.mailbag/1.html |archive-date=October 26, 2012}} Green won the 2005 [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big East Rookie of the Year]] award along with [[Rudy Gay]] of the [[University of Connecticut]]. He was named to the [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] Second Team in 2006 along with teammate Roy Hibbert. In 2007, Green was named the Big East Player of the Year. He and Hibbert were unanimous selections to the All-Big East First Team. After his 30-point performance in the [[2007 Big East men's basketball tournament|2007 Big East tournament]] semifinal against [[2006–07 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]]{{Cite web |date=2007-03-09 |title=Green's Jumper with 13 Seconds Left Lifts Top-Seeded Georgetown Past Notre Dame, 84-82, as Hoyas Advance to BIG EAST Championship Game |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2007/3/9/Green_s_Jumper_with_13_Seconds_Left_Lifts_Top_Seeded_Georgetown_Past_Notre_Dame_84_82_as_Hoyas_Advance_to_BIG_EAST_Championship_Game.aspx |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=Georgetown University Athletics |language=en}} and his 21-point performance in the championship against [[2006–07 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]],{{Cite web |date=2007-03-10 |title=No. 9 Georgetown Handles No. 13 Pittsburgh, 65-42, To Claim Big East Tournament Crown |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2007/3/10/No_9_Georgetown_Handles_No_13_Pittsburgh_65_42_To_Claim_Big_East_Tournament_Crown.aspx |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=Georgetown University Athletics |language=en}} Green was named Most Outstanding Player of the tournament, as the Hoyas won their first Big East title since 1989. He led the Hoyas to the Final Four of the [[2007 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2007 NCAA tournament]], beating [[2006–07 Belmont Bruins men's basketball team|Belmont]]{{Cite web |date=2007-03-15 |title=Sapp's Career-High 20 Points Leads No. 2 Georgetown Past Belmont, 80-55 |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2007/3/15/Sapp_s_Career_High_20_Points_Leads_No_2_Georgetown_Past_Belmont_80_55.aspx |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=Georgetown University Athletics |language=en}} and [[2006–07 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]]{{Cite web |date=2007-03-17 |title=How Sweet It Is! Hoyas Power Past Eagles In Second Round Of NCAA Tourney, 62-55 |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2007/3/17/How_Sweet_It_Is_Hoyas_Power_Past_Eagles_In_Second_Round_Of_NCAA_Tourney_62_55.aspx |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=Georgetown University Athletics |language=en}} in the first two rounds. Green helped Georgetown beat [[2006–07 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] with a game-winning shot after a controversial no-call in the game's closing seconds{{Cite web |date=2007-03-23 |title=Green's Jumper with 2.5 Seconds Left Carries Georgetown to 66-65 Win Over Vanderbilt and Into NCAA Tournament Elite Eight |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2007/3/23/Green_s_Jumper_with_2_5_Seconds_Left_Carries_Georgetown_to_66_65_Win_Over_Vanderbilt_and_Into_NCAA_Tournament_Elite_Eight.aspx |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=Georgetown University Athletics |language=en}} as well as fearlessly leading the Hoyas to victory against No. 1 seed [[2006–07 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|UNC]] in a stunning second-half comeback victory and bringing the Hoyas back to their first Final Four since [[Patrick Ewing]] led them to the 1985 national championship game.{{Cite web |date=2007-03-25 |title=Georgetown Puts Away Top-Seeded North Carolina In OT, 96-84; Earns First Trip To Final Four Since 1985 |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2007/3/25/Georgetown_Puts_Away_Top_Seeded_North_Carolina_In_OT_96_84_Earns_First_Trip_To_Final_Four_Since_1985.aspx |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=Georgetown University Athletics |language=en}} The Hoyas eventually lost to [[Greg Oden]] and [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]],{{Cite web |date=2007-03-31 |title=Georgetown's Championship Run Halted By Ohio State, 67-60, In National Semifinal |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2007/3/31/Georgetown_s_Championship_Run_Halted_By_Ohio_State_67_60_In_National_Semifinal.aspx |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=Georgetown University Athletics |language=en}} bringing their remarkable title run to a close as well as Green's collegiate playing career, as he chose to forgo his senior year and entered the [[NBA draft]]. Green spent the next four summers taking classes at Georgetown and graduated in 2012 with a degree in English and a minor in theology.{{cite news |last=Steinberg |first=Dan |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/dc-sports-bog/post/jeff-green-on-graduating-from-georgetown/2012/05/17/gIQAUB67VU_blog.html |title=Jeff Green on graduating from Georgetown |newspaper=The Washington Post|date=May 17, 2012 |access-date=October 28, 2013}} ==Professional career== ===Seattle SuperSonics/Oklahoma City Thunder (2007–2011)=== On June 28, 2007, Green was selected with the fifth overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. He was later traded to the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] alongside [[Wally Szczerbiak]] and [[Delonte West]] in exchange for [[Ray Allen]] and [[Glen Davis (basketball)|Glen Davis]].{{cite web |date=June 28, 2007 |others=Contributed by The Associated Press |title=Sonics' Allen traded to Celts for Wally, West & Green |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2920183 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}} On April 6, 2008, Green scored a then career-high 35 points against the [[Denver Nuggets]]. Green made the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] in 2008 after averaging 10.5 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 80 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/greenje02/gamelog/2008/|title=Jeff Green 2007–08 game log|work=Basketball-Reference|access-date=August 10, 2018}} The Sonics were sold and moved to [[Oklahoma City]] before the start of the 2008–09 season, becoming the Thunder. In January 2009, Green hit his first career game-winner, lifting the Thunder to a 122–121 victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|last=Mayberry|first=Darnell|url=https://newsok.com/article/3339822/jeff-greens-shot-lifts-oklahoma-city-thunder|title=Jeff Green's shot lifts Oklahoma City Thunder|work=newsok.com|date=January 22, 2009|access-date=August 10, 2018}} In the 2009–10 season, Green played and started in all 82 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/greenje02/gamelog/2010/|title=Jeff Green 2009–10 game log|work=Basketball-Reference|access-date=August 10, 2018}} On December 1, 2010, he set a new career high with 37 points against the [[New Jersey Nets]]. ===Boston Celtics (2011–2015)=== [[File:Jeff green celtics 1.jpg|thumb|right|Green in April 2011]] [[File:Jeff Green in March 2013.jpg|thumb|right|Green in March 2013]] On February 24, 2011, Green was traded, along with [[Nenad Krstić]] and a 2012 first-round pick, to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Kendrick Perkins]] and [[Nate Robinson]].{{cite web |date=February 24, 2011 |title=Thunder Acquires Perkins and Robinson |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_trade1_110224.html |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}}{{cite web |last1=Ford |first1=Chad |last2=Sheridan |first2=Chris |name-list-style=and |date=February 25, 2011 |title=Celtics get Thunder's Jeff Green |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/news/story?id=6155082 |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}} Green recorded a double-double in his first start as a Celtic against the [[Washington Wizards]] on April 11, recording 20 points, a career-high-tying 15 rebounds, four assists and two steals. Green improved his field goal percentage after the trade to the Celtics, shooting 48.5 percent from the floor in 26 games after shooting 43.7 percent with the Thunder.{{cite web |last=Stringer |first=Pete |date=December 10, 2011 |title=Celtics Re-Sign Jeff Green |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press121011-celtics-resign-jeff-green.html |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} On December 10, 2011, following the conclusion of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]], Green re-signed with the Celtics on a one-year, $9 million contract. Eight days later, his contract was voided by the Celtics after a routine physical examination detected an [[aortic aneurysm]].{{cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=December 18, 2011 |others=Contributed by The Associated Press |title=Jeff Green to have heart surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/story/_/id/7362378 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}} Green subsequently underwent heart surgery in January 2012 and missed the entire 2011–12 season.{{cite web|last=May|first=Peter|url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/story/_/id/7433745/boston-celtics-withdrew-qualifying-offer-jeff-green-now-ufa|title=Celts pulled Jeff Green qualifying offer|work=ESPN.com|date=January 6, 2012|access-date=August 10, 2018}} Former teammate [[Kevin Durant]] dedicated his season to Green.{{cite web |last=Holmes |first=Baxter |date=June 8, 2018 |title=How Jeff Green returned from a heart defect that almost ended his life |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23713648 |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=ESPN.com |quote=In 2011-2012, while Green had been sidelined, Kevin Durant had dedicated the season to his former teammate.}} Green used his downtime not only to rehab from surgery but to complete his coursework at Georgetown, graduating in May 2012 with a degree in English and a minor in theology. On August 22, 2012, Green re-signed with the Celtics on a four-year, $36 million contract.{{cite web |last=D'Amico |first=Marc |date=August 22, 2012 |title=Celtics Sign Jeff Green |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/082212-celtics-sign-jeff-green.html |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}}{{cite web |last=Payne |first=Gregg |date=August 23, 2012 |title=Jeff Green's Celtics deal is official |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/story/_/id/8294323 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}} On March 18, 2013, he scored a career-high 43 points in a 105–103 loss to the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=March 18, 2013 |title=Jeff Green wins 'em over in loss |url=https://www.espn.com.au/boston/nba/story/_/id/9069399 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}}{{cite web |last=Robb |first=Brian |date=March 19, 2013 |title=Notebook: Heat 105, Celtics 103 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130318/MIABOS/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203095851/http://www.nba.com/games/20130318/MIABOS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |access-date=October 28, 2013 |work=NBA.com}} On April 3, Green scored 34 points against the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/greenje02/gamelog/2013/|title=Jeff Green 2012–13 game log|work=Basketball-Reference|access-date=August 10, 2018}} In 2013–14, Green played and started in all 82 games for the Celtics following the departure of [[Paul Pierce]] and [[Kevin Garnett]] in the off-season. He subsequently had a career-best season as he averaged a career-high 16.9 points per game. On January 22, Green scored 39 points against the Wizards. On March 16 against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], he had a second 39-point game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/greenje02/gamelog/2014/|title=Jeff Green 2013–14 game log|work=Basketball-Reference|access-date=August 10, 2018}} Over the first two months of the 2014–15 season, Green averaged a career-best 17.6 points per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/greenje02/gamelog/2015/|title=Jeff Green 2014–15 game log|work=Basketball-Reference|access-date=August 10, 2018}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2015–2016)=== On January 12, 2015, Green was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a three-team deal involving the Celtics and the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |date=January 12, 2015 |title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Jeff Green and Russ Smith in three-team trade with Boston Celtics and New Orleans Pelicans |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-green-smith-three-team-trade-150112 |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} He made his Grizzlies debut two days later, recording 10 points and three rebounds off the bench in a 103–92 victory over the Brooklyn Nets.{{cite web |last=Mahoney |first=Brian |date=January 15, 2015 |title=Grizzlies rout Nets in first matchup with ex-coach Hollins |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150114/MEMBKN/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114170053/http://www.nba.com/games/20150114/MEMBKN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 14, 2016 |access-date=January 15, 2015 |work=NBA.com}} On June 18, Green exercised his player option with the Grizzlies for the 2015–16 season.{{cite web |date=June 18, 2015 |title=Jeff Green exercises Player Option for 2015-16 Season |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/jeff-green-exercises-player-option-150618 |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} On December 13, 2015, Green scored a season-high 26 points in a loss to the Miami Heat.{{cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=December 13, 2015 |title=Wade leads rally, Heat beat Grizzlies 100–97 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151213/MEMMIA/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151215232908/http://www.nba.com/games/20151213/MEMMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 15, 2015 |access-date=December 13, 2015 |work=NBA.com}} He topped that mark on January 25, 2016, scoring 30 points off the bench in a 108–102 overtime victory over the Orlando Magic. In that game, Green converted an 11-footer with 1.3 seconds left for a 100–100 tie at the end of regulation.{{cite web |date=January 26, 2016 |title=Magic @ Grizzlies |url=https://www.nba.com/game/orl-vs-mem-0021500670/box-score |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2016)=== On February 18, 2016, Green was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Lance Stephenson]] and a future protected first-round pick.{{cite web |last=Dixon |first=Robyn |date=February 18, 2016 |title=LA Clippers Acquire Jeff Green From Memphis |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-acquire-jeff-green-from-memphis |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} Two days later, he made his Clippers debut in a 115–112 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]], recording five points, two rebounds and one assist in 20 minutes off the bench.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160220/GSWLAC/gameinfo.html |title=Warriors ride hot shooting to 115–112 victory over Clippers |work=NBA.com |date=February 20, 2016 |access-date=February 20, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229100226/http://www.nba.com/games/20160220/GSWLAC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 29, 2018 |url-status=dead }} On February 26, Green made his first start for the Clippers, scoring 22 points in 31 minutes of action in a 117–107 victory over the Sacramento Kings.{{cite web |last=Weidel |first=Jeffrey |date=February 27, 2016 |title=Paul has 40 points, 13 assists as Clippers top Kings 117–107 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160226/LACSAC/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160228091806/http://www.nba.com/games/20160226/LACSAC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=February 28, 2016 |access-date=February 27, 2016 |work=NBA.com}} ===Orlando Magic (2016–2017)=== On July 7, 2016, Green signed a one-year, $15 million contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web |last=Denton |first=John |url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-jeff-green |title=Orlando Magic Sign Jeff Green |work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2016 |access-date=July 7, 2016}} He made his Magic debut in their season opener on October 26, scoring seven points off the bench in a 108–96 loss to the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899378 |title=Heat vs. Magic – Box Score |work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016 |access-date=October 26, 2016}} On April 5, 2017, Green was shut down for the rest of the season due to lower back soreness that plagued him throughout the season.{{cite web |last=Robbins |first=Josh |date=April 5, 2017 |title=Jeff Green says Magic plan to shut him down remainder of season |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2017/04/05/jeff-green-says-magic-plan-to-shut-him-down-remainder-of-season/ |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=OrlandoSentinel.com}} Green missed the final nine games of the season.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900595 |title=Orlando hangs on to defeat Detroit 113–109 |work=ESPN.com |date=April 12, 2017 |access-date=April 13, 2017}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2017–2018)=== On July 11, 2017, Green signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on a minimum contract.{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Nick |date=July 11, 2017 |title=Cavaliers Sign Jeff Green |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/green-signing-2017 |access-date=October 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} On May 27, 2018, he scored 19 points starting in place of the injured [[Kevin Love]], helping the Cavaliers defeat the Celtics in Game 7 of the Eastern [[NBA Conference finals|Conference finals]].{{Cite news |last=Yang |first=Nicole |date=May 28, 2018 |title=Jeff Green on his Game 7 performance: 'It means a lot' |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2018/05/28/celtics-cavs-jeff-green-game-7/ |access-date=November 21, 2018 |work=Boston.com |language=en-US}} The Cavaliers played the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2018 NBA Finals]], where they were defeated in four games.{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2018/06/08/warriors-dynasty-historic-sweep-lebron-james-cavaliers-nba-finals/687107002/|title=Warriors earn dynasty with historic sweep of LeBron James, Cavaliers|work=USA Today|last=Zillgitt|first=Jeff|date=June 8, 2018|access-date=February 20, 2023|location=Cleveland}} ===Washington Wizards (2018–2019)=== [[File:Jeff Green (50595057928).jpg|thumb|Green in 2018]] On July 10, 2018, Green signed with his hometown team the [[Washington Wizards]] on a minimum contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2018/07/10/digest-july-10-wizards-make-it-official-sign-forward-jeff-green/|title=Digest (July 10): Wizards make it official, sign forward Jeff Green|work=baltimoresun.com|date=July 10, 2018|access-date=July 10, 2018}} He made his Wizards debut on October 18, recording 17 points and four rebounds in a narrow 113–112 loss to the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |date=October 19, 2018 |title=Olynyk's putback off Wade's miss lifts Heat past Wiz 113-112 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401070702 |access-date=January 25, 2023 |website=ESPN}} On February 4, 2019, Green scored a season-high 26 points, alongside five rebounds and five assists, in a 137–129 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |date=February 5, 2019 |title=Prince, Huerter lead Hawks to 137-129 win over Wizards |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071464 |access-date=January 25, 2023 |website=ESPN |agency=The Associated Press}} ===Utah Jazz (2019)=== On July 20, 2019, Green signed a one-year, minimum deal with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |last=Falk |first=Aaron |date=July 20, 2019 |title=Jazz Sign Ed Davis, Jeff Green and Emmanuel
